scope: PR #1877 S16d r2, hi/ui.common.time: the 4 landed keys (today_at, yesterday, weekday_at, date_at) after the round-1 correction, judged on composed Intl output through formatDividerLabel; key_count 5

findings.observation: Round-1 MAJOR (stub-identical to English) is resolved: '{weekday} को {time}' composes as 'सोमवार को 2:30 pm'. को after a weekday name is the standard Hindi 'on Monday'; it is grammatical and idiomatic for a terse divider and does not read as a calque.

'{date} को {time}' composes as '5 नवंबर 2026 को 2:30 pm'. Date + को + clock is standard Hindi date-time phrasing; a comma joiner would also be acceptable, but को is not wrong for a past date and needs no replacement.
'आज {time}' with no को is correct and consistent: आज/कल are time adverbs taking no postposition, while weekday names and dates take को. The difference is grammatical, not an inconsistency.

बजे is deliberately absent: the injected {time} is the Intl hi clock '2:30 pm', so appending बजे would read '2:30 pm बजे'. Consistent with today_at/yesterday_at, which were audited in an earlier round.
'कल' also means 'tomorrow', the language's own ambiguity; in a past-message meta row the context disambiguates and no better single word exists, so it is not a defect.
